panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A is a histology image from a patient with Buerger's disease showing fibrinoid necrosis in the intima and media of a small to medium-sized artery, consistent with the caption and article context. B: Panel B is a histology image showing fibrinoid necrosis in a medium-sized vein, a finding consistent with thromboangiitis obliterans as stated in the caption. C: Panel C shows a mixed inflammatory infiltrate involving all layers of the vessel wall (intima, media, adventitia), which is a hallmark histologic finding of thromboangiitis obliterans and matches the vocabulary term for transmural vascular inflammation. D: Panel D shows a vein with a luminal thrombus (star), a finding consistent with thromboangiitis obliterans as part of the histologic spectrum in the case. The thrombus is not further characterized as inflammatory in the caption, so it is proposed as a finding.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a real patient's left foot. The caption and in-text describe tissue necrosis with exposed bone on the hallux in a 28-year-old chronic smoker with absent distal pulses, in an article specifically about thromboangiitis obliterans; the visible black necrotic hallux with ulceration and exposed bone is a specific clinical manifestation (digital ischemic necrosis/gangrene) of the configured target disease, not a diagram, control, or other disease. A: PAS stain (X10) of a small artery from a TAO patient untreated for many years; perivascular inflammatory infiltrate with a preserved vessel wall and early thrombus is the histopathology of TAO itself, as stated in the caption. A: H&E histopathology of superior mesenteric artery wall from a patient with Buerger's disease (article title and prior triage confirm thromboangiitis_obliterans in a real patient). In-text: 'marked intimal hyperplasia and inflammatory infiltration'; residual lumen narrowed by hypercellular inflamed intimal tissue (visual).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: H&E histopathology of excised human internal thoracic artery intima from a histopathologically confirmed coronary TAO case (article title and in-text confirmation). Shows marked concentric intimal thickening, perivascular lymphocytic infiltration, and a distinct internal elastic lamina consistent with TAO rather than atherosclerosis. Coronary/thoracic involvement is an unusual site for TAO, so the presentation is atypical. B: Longitudinal H&E section of the coronary arterial plug from the same confirmed TAO case, showing identical intimal hyperplasia with surface inflammatory infiltrate; human patient tissue with disease attribution supported by the article title and in-text confirmation.
